newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - AEA sees three tracks to future.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - AEA sees three tracks to future.

text.p: British science and nuclear technology company AEA Technology Plc sees further growth from acquisitions and from existing business as well as through partnerships, chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I think we can see further growth coming both organically and from through acquisitions, we'll take the opportunities wherever we find them," he said on Monday.
He said each potential acquisition would be taken on its own merits and that with gearing at around 25 percent, "I think we have headroom if we find the right opportunity."
But he added that "in some areas, I think particularly internationally, the idea of partnership is very attractive and I'm sure we'll develop that."

AEA Technology, privatised from the state-owned Atomic Energy Authority last year, saw pre-tax profits for its first year as a quoted company of 18.5 million stg, up from 15.8 million, and paid out a total dividend of 8.4 pence per share.
Operating profits were up 22 percent to 24.1 million stg with turnover rising four percent to 264 million.
Cleaver said the growth in turnover masked a decline in business from the Atomic Energy Authority offset by gains in the private sector both here and overseas.
"The UK private sector has gone up by 18 percent and our overseas business...by 34 percent," he said.
He said that he was encouraged the increase in profits had come from "better margins and also from those higher sales," not just from cutting costs.
Cleaver said AEA Technology also saw further possibilities for partnerships with companies.

"We see opportunities for working with major companies in many cases who have some aspect of their business where either we've got particular expertise or basically (they) don't want to do it in house any longer," he said.
